links.outcome: Institution-specific recalibration of NTCP model parameters versus published QUANTEC values
links.effect: Institutional parotid TD50 34.1 Gy vs QUANTEC 39.0 Gy (m 0.11 vs 0.18); traditional models performed acceptably after local calibration (LKB AUC 0.88-0.91).
links.quote: In particular, the parotid TD50 was estimated at 34.1 Gy, compared with 39.0 Gy reported in QUANTEC, with a corresponding slope parameter m of 0.11 versus 0.18 as shown in the institute-specific dose-response curves ( Figure 4 ).

links.outcome: Agreement between two independent NTCP computational pipelines against predefined acceptance criteria
links.effect: Mean bias 0.8%, 95% limits of agreement -1.9% to +3.5%, meeting predefined criteria (bias <3%, limits within ±5%); max deviation 2.4%.
links.quote: The mean bias was 0.8%, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from −1.9% to +3.5%, meeting the predefined acceptability criteria (mean bias <3% and limits within ±5%).

links.outcome: ANN and XGBoost versus best traditional NTCP model (LKB) discrimination on hold-out test set
links.effect: ANN AUC 0.93 vs LKB 0.89 (p=0.420) parotid; 0.95 vs 0.91 (p=0.380) oral cavity; 0.91 vs 0.88 (p=0.150) larynx; no significant differences; XGBoost overfit (test AUC 0.67-0.82).
links.quote: No statistically significant differences were observed between ANN and the best traditional model (LKB) for any organ.

links.effect: XGBoost training AUC 0.98–1.00 fell to test AUC 0.67–0.82, showing overfitting.
links.quote: Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models showed lower generalisation performance compared with ANN across all endpoints, with evidence of overfitting despite regularisation (training AUC 0.98–1.00; test AUC 0.67–0.82).

links.effect: Accuracy 85.0%–94.1% mostly reflected predicting absence of Grade ≥2 toxicity, not clinical utility.
links.quote: Reported accuracy values (85.0%–94.1%) largely reflected correct classification of the majority class (absence of Grade ≥ 2 toxicity) and were therefore not interpreted as indicators of clinical utility in the context of severe class imbalance [ 51 ].

links.effect: ANN ΔAUC was +0.04 parotid, +0.04 oral cavity, +0.03 larynx; no significant advantage.
links.quote: When comparing ANN against the best-performing traditional model (LKB) for each organ, differences were modest across all endpoints: parotid glands (ΔAUC +0.04), oral cavity (ΔAUC +0.04) and mixed-architecture larynx (ΔAUC +0.03), no statistically significant advantage for ML was observed for any organ architecture.

links.effect: Local LKB AUCs were 0.89 parotid, 0.88 laryngeal, and 0.91 oral cavity.
links.quote: The LKB probit model demonstrated the highest discrimination across all three endpoints, with AUC values of 0.89 for parotid toxicity, 0.88 for laryngeal toxicity and 0.91 for oral cavity toxicity, although confidence intervals were wide owing to the limited number of events.

links.effect: Local TD50 was lower than QUANTEC: parotid 34.1 vs 39.0 Gy, oral 48.5 vs 50.0, larynx 43.6 vs 46.0.
links.quote: Institution-specific LKB parameter estimates differed systematically from QUANTEC-recommended values across organs, with lower TD50 estimates observed for the parotid glands (34.1 Gy versus QUANTEC 39.0 Gy), oral cavity (48.5 Gy versus 50.0 Gy) and larynx (43.6 Gy versus 46.0 Gy).

links.effect: After local calibration, LKB had AUC 0.88–0.91 and institution-specific parameters differed from QUANTEC.
links.quote: Following local calibration, traditional radiobiological models demonstrated robust toxicity risk stratification, with the LKB model achieving the highest discrimination (AUC 0.88–0.91) and institution-specific parameters differing from QUANTEC values.
